newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian minister says not to meet Commonwealth.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian minister says not to meet Commonwealth.

text.p: Nigeria's Foreign Minister Tom Ikimi on Monday said he had no plans to meet Commonwealth officials who are pushing for a human rights probe.
"They have not asked to see me, and why should they? They are here to discuss with officials the modalities and dates for the ministerial level meeting," Ikimi told Reuters.
"This was set out in the letter which they sent explaining their mission,"
A team of four Commonwealth officials, led by Deputy Secretary-General Srina Vasan, went into a meeting behind closed doors in the capital with Nigerian officials.
Commonwealth ministers last month agreed to send the officials to pave the way for a ministerial level mission, after a proposed visit was called off when Nigeria imposed strict conditions.

Nigeria insists the only matter for discussion is Nigeria's suspension from the Commonwealth, and says the organisation has no right to send the fact-finding mission on human rights and democracy it has requested.
"Our position on the mandate of the Commonwealth remains clear and has not changed," Ikimi said. REUTER MT
